The Word gives an itinerary heading for Foz de Iguazu, with no equivalent highlights heading.

blocks.text: At Iguazu, you hear the falls before you see them. The steady roar reaches you first, then mist rises above the canyon and the cascades come into view. The Brazilian side gives you a view of the entire waterfall system. Optional tours take you closer to the region’s wildlife and landscapes. Macuco Safari combines a ride through the forest with a speedboat trip by the falls. At the Bird Park, you can walk through large aviaries among toucans, macaws and flamingos.

Word has a day heading for the Pantanal, but no equivalent wildlife highlights heading.

blocks.text: The Pantanal is prized for its open landscapes. In dense tropical forest, an animal can disappear from view in seconds. On these plains and beside the water, you can spend longer watching caimans, capybaras, anteaters and birds. Routes depend on the season, water levels and weather, so guides choose the areas with the best chance of sightings each day. Early morning is an especially good time to look.
